comparator.name: Notarieel Recht
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from VU Amsterdam's current official sources for the Fall-2026 cohort: the Notarieel Recht programme content page, the programme's 2026-2027 Onderwijs- en Examenregeling (OER B NOT 2026-2027), and the career/'toekomst' page. Article 10.2 (Afstudeerrichtingen) records 'n.v.t.': the programme has no formal specialisations/routes. Articles 12.1-12.2 (Vrije keuzeruimte; Minoren) likewise record 'n.v.t.', and Article 2.2.1.c explicitly excludes Notarieel Recht from the faculty's general 30-EC keuzeruimte requirement that applies to other law-faculty bachelors. The programme content page confirms this in plain language: 'De bachelor Notarieel Recht bestaat daarom uitsluitend uit verplichte vakken' (the bachelor consists exclusively of compulsory courses), organised around three professional pillars -- onroerend goedrecht (real-estate law), familierecht (family law) and ondernemingsrecht (business/corporate law) -- with tax law as a compulsory (not elective) third-year specialisation. There is therefore no open elective/profiling space to preserve as a component. Year 1 (60 EC, Article 11.3, studiejaar 2026-2027) is identical to the general Rechtsgeleerdheid bachelor's first year and is unaffected by any later change: Beginselen bestuursrecht (6), Beginselen Europees recht (6), Beginselen staatsrecht (6), Beginselen strafrecht (6), Encyclopedie der rechtswetenschap I (6, academische kern), Inleiding goederenrecht (3), Inleiding in de rechtswetenschap (6), Inleiding verbintenissenrecht (6), Juridische vaardigheden (6, embeds the PPI-1 professional-identity leerlijn and a compulsory Dutch-language diagnostic test, neither separately credited), Personen- en familierecht (3), and Rechtsgeschiedenis (6, academische kern). The OER's Article 15.2 overgangsbepalingen state explicitly that a curriculum change to years 2 and 3, effective per studiejaar 2027-2028, applies 'in principe... voor de studenten die in studiejaar 2026-2027 starten met de bachelor' (in principle to students who start the bachelor in academic year 2026-2027) -- i.e. to exactly the Fall-2026 cohort used for this comparison. This reconstruction therefore uses the year-2 and year-3 tables the OER itself labels 'per studiejaar 2027-2028' (further refined only in period placement, not credits, by the OER's studiejaar-2028-2029 transition entries), rather than the tables labelled 'studiejaar 2026-2027' that apply only to students who started in 2025-2026 or earlier. Year 2 (60 EC) under this table: Bestuursrecht (6, embeds the PPI-2 leerlijn, not separately credited), Burgerlijk procesrecht en insolventieprocesrecht (6), Contractenrecht (6), Erfrecht I (6), Formeel strafrecht (6), Goederenrecht (6), Materieel strafrecht (6), Vennootschaps- en rechtspersonenrecht (6), Verbreding goederenrecht A (6), and Volkenrecht (6). Year 3 (60 EC) under the same table: Bachelorscriptie (6; Article 9.1 permits enrolment only after 120 EC including Juridische vaardigheden is completed), Bedrijfseconomie I (6), Elementair belastingrecht (6), Erfrecht II (6, moved from year 2), Notariële ambtsuitoefening (6, moved from year 2), Ondernemingsrecht (6), Pleitoefening (6; the programme content page specifies this course offers an optional notarial track, 'Notariële conflictoplossing', focused on conflict analysis and negotiation), Relatievermogensrecht (9), Verbreding goederenrecht B (3), and Verdieping belastingrecht (6). No OER article or further official source needed to be consulted beyond the programme content page, the OER and the career page: together they establish a complete, internally consistent, entirely compulsory 180-EC pathway with explicit EC weights for every component and an explicit route/elective judgment (n.v.t. to both) that was fixed before any UCR course was considered.

alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to VU's fully compulsory Notarieel Recht bachelor (OER Article 10.2 confirms no formal afstudeerrichtingen exist, and Articles 12.1-12.2 confirm no free-elective or minor space: the programme 'bestaat uitsluitend uit verplichte vakken'). It reproduces as far as UCR allows the programme's three professional pillars -- real-estate/property law, family relationships and private law, and business/corporate law -- together with the compulsory third-year tax-law specialisation, notarial professional practice and the notarial conflict-resolution/negotiation track within pleading practice, and the case-law/statute analysis and legal-argument construction trained throughout the legal-skills and pleading sequence. It combines UCR's full available law cluster (Law, Society & Justice and all six GOSLAWJ courses) with UCR's business, entrepreneurship, finance and economics courses (standing in for VU's business/corporate-law and tax-law content), a dedicated negotiation course and organisational-psychology and persuasive-communication courses (standing in for the notarial conflict-resolution track and legal-argumentation skills), and a research-methods course. It leaves an honest gap where UCR has no course of any kind: dedicated inheritance/succession, matrimonial-property, Dutch tax-law doctrine, civil-procedure/insolvency and notarial-office-practice content are not offered at UCR at any level of depth.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum combines UCR's full available law cluster (7 of 24 courses: Law, Society & Justice and all six GOSLAWJ courses, covering property, contract, family-adjacent, criminal, constitutional, EU and international law) in roughly equal measure with UCR's business, entrepreneurship and finance cluster (7 of 24 courses, covering business formation, company law, transnational business law and finance), supported by economics (including UCR's closest available counterpart to taxation), organisational psychology, a dedicated negotiation course and persuasive-communication courses. The label names Private Law first, matching VU's own private-law-centred professional identity; Business second for the company/commercial-law strand that recurs throughout VU's own business, corporate and tax components; and Negotiation third for the notarial conflict-resolution and pleading-practice content that UCR's dedicated Negotiation & Strategic Thinking course most directly implements. It does not claim a dedicated inheritance, estate-planning, matrimonial-property or Dutch tax-law doctrine that the completed 24-course curriculum does not contain.

progressionAssessment.rationale: GOSGATE102 and BENGATE101 (both no-prerequisite gateway courses) are scheduled in semester 1, before every course that formally requires them: GOSLAWJ211/212/213/311/312 (semesters 2-3) and BENBUSI311/312, BENENTR212/311/312 (semesters 2, 4-6) are all scheduled after their respective gateway. BENGATE102 (Research Methods & Statistics) is scheduled in semester 2, before every course that formally requires it: BENLEAD311 (semester 3), BENECON311 and BENLEAD312 (semester 4) and BENECON212 (semester 6). Level-1 gateway and introductory courses are concentrated in semesters 1-3 (Law, Society & Justice, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Rhetorical Communication, Research Methods & Statistics, Introduction to Economics), and level-3 advanced law, business, tax and negotiation work is concentrated in semesters 3-6 (Principles of Private Law, Transnational Business Law, Public Economics, Negotiation & Strategic Thinking, Persuasive Communication, Money Banking & Finance, Market Research), so that foundational legal and business training precedes advanced applied work. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 1, within year 1. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match directly owns eight generator-eligible rows: the preventive, fair-agreement conception of notarial law (5003, 5004); family relationships, inheritance and estate planning (5005); property, real estate and ownership (5007); notarial conflict resolution and negotiation (5009); legal analysis of statutes and judgments (5010); building and defending legal arguments (5011); and private law as the broad foundation (5012). The remaining two generator-eligible rows -- business formation and corporate law (5006) and tax law in private and business transactions (5008) -- were independently assessed as their own candidate direction, Business, Corporate & Tax Law for Notarial and Commercial Practice, supported by the corporate/legal-entity-law and business-economics curricular-topic rows (5017, 5021), since VU's own programme names business/corporate law as one of three professional pillars alongside real-estate and family law. Current official evidence confirms these are not separable routes, however: OER Article 10.2 records no afstudeerrichtingen, Articles 12.1-12.2 record no vrije keuzeruimte or minoren, and the programme's own description frames real-estate law, family law and business law as three pillars of one indivisible compulsory curriculum, with tax law as a compulsory (not elective) third-year specialisation. Every UCR course that concretely addresses business formation, company law or taxation -- Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Accounting & Corporate Finance, Transnational Business Law, Money, Banking & Finance, Strategy & Digital Transformation, Market Research, International Business & Governance, Introduction to Economics, Microeconomics & Behavior and Public Economics -- is already used by the closest match, because these are the only business/tax-adjacent courses UCR's actual catalogue contains. A second alternative built around this candidate would therefore either reuse at least twenty of the closest match's own courses (far short of the required 30-EC/4-course floor) or substitute courses with no evidenced connection to business or tax at all. Because the candidate's own evidence is already substantively covered by courses the closest match already contains and no genuinely different 24-course curriculum follows from it given UCR's actual offerings, it is rejected as not-substantively-distinct rather than manufactured through arbitrary course substitution, and production stops at one included alternative.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both are the introductory orientation course to law that every student takes before any specialist course: Inleiding in de rechtswetenschap is VU's broad introduction to legal science; Law, Society & Justice is UCR's own introduction to law from legal, social and normative perspectives, including explicit coverage of property, contract and tort.

Both develop the construction, evaluation and presentation of persuasive, evidence-based arguments in writing and speech; UCR teaches this through rhetoric rather than specifically legal documents, while Juridische vaardigheden also embeds the PPI-1 professional-identity leerlijn and a Dutch-language diagnostic test.

Encyclopedie der rechtswetenschap I is a dedicated legal-science methodology and systematics course. UCR's own introductory law course, Law, Society & Justice, is already aligned to Inleiding in de rechtswetenschap above and cannot be matched twice, and UCR offers no separate legal-methodology course, so no counterpart is claimed.

Rechtsgeschiedenis is a dedicated legal-history course. UCR offers no legal-history course; its law-track courses discuss historical context in passing but do not reproduce a dedicated legal-history unit.
Both are the programme's foundational EU-law course, covering the EU legal order, institutions and the internal market.

Both examine constitutional law and state organisation; Comparative Constitutional Law does so through a comparative five-country approach, while Beginselen staatsrecht is VU's own introductory constitutional-law course.
Both introduce public international law's sources, institutions and treaty practice; Volkenrecht is VU's own dedicated public-international-law course.

Beginselen bestuursrecht is a dedicated introductory administrative-law course. Comparative Constitutional Law is already aligned to the comparator's constitutional-law component above and cannot be matched twice, and UCR offers no separate administrative-law course, so no counterpart is claimed.

Bestuursrecht is VU's second, more advanced administrative-law course. UCR's only constitutional/administrative-law course is already matched to the first-year component above; UCR does not offer a second, more advanced course, so no further counterpart is claimed.
Both are the programme's introductory criminal-law course, covering criminal accountability, guilt, legality and the justification of punishment.

Formeel strafrecht is a dedicated criminal-procedure course. UCR's only criminal-law course, Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, is already matched to the introductory component above; UCR does not offer a separate procedural criminal-law course, so no further counterpart is claimed.

Materieel strafrecht is a dedicated advanced substantive criminal-law course. UCR's only criminal-law course is already matched above and cannot be matched twice, so no further counterpart is claimed.

Both introduce property law as part of a broader private-law survey; Principles of Private Law examines property law, tort law and contract law together with the rights and obligations arising from family, landlord-tenant and neighbour relationships, and property is the field named first in its own course description.

Inleiding verbintenissenrecht is VU's dedicated introductory obligations/contract-law course. UCR's Principles of Private Law, which also covers contract law, is already aligned to the property-law component above and cannot be matched twice, so no further counterpart is claimed.

Personen- en familierecht is a dedicated family-law course. Principles of Private Law mentions family relationships only as an illustrative example and is already matched above; UCR offers no dedicated family-law course, so this is an honest gap despite family being a top direct programme interest.
Contractenrecht is VU's dedicated advanced contract-law course. UCR's Principles of Private Law, already matched above, does not reproduce a second, more advanced contract-law course.
Goederenrecht is VU's dedicated advanced property-law course. UCR's Principles of Private Law is already matched to the introductory property component above and cannot be matched twice.
Verbreding goederenrecht A further extends property law. UCR offers only one course touching property law, already matched above, so no further counterpart is claimed.
Verbreding goederenrecht B further extends property law in year 3. UCR's single property-adjacent course is already matched above.
Erfrecht I is a dedicated introductory inheritance/succession-law course. UCR offers no inheritance or succession-law course of any kind, so no counterpart is claimed.
Erfrecht II is a dedicated advanced inheritance/succession-law course. UCR offers no inheritance or succession-law course of any kind.

Relatievermogensrecht (matrimonial/relationship property law) is a dedicated course combining family and property law at an advanced level. UCR offers no matrimonial-property course; its closest private-law course is already matched above.

Burgerlijk procesrecht en insolventieprocesrecht is a dedicated civil-procedure and insolvency-law course. UCR offers no course in civil procedure or insolvency law of any kind, so no counterpart is claimed.

Both apply legal reasoning to business organisation and transactions: Transnational Business Law surveys company law, contracts law, trade law, intellectual property and dispute resolution; Ondernemingsrecht is VU's dedicated corporate/enterprise-law course.

Vennootschaps- en rechtspersonenrecht is a dedicated company and legal-entity-law course. UCR's Transnational Business Law, which also covers company law, is already aligned to the comparator's corporate-law component above and cannot be matched twice, so no further counterpart is claimed.

Both address business/financial-management content: Accounting & Corporate Finance teaches reading and analysing corporate financial statements; Bedrijfseconomie I is VU's dedicated business-economics course.

Both examine taxation and government revenue; Public Economics analyses taxation, public spending and redistribution from an economic-policy perspective, UCR's closest available counterpart to VU's own tax-law course, though it does not teach tax-law doctrine, sources or procedure.

Verdieping belastingrecht is VU's dedicated advanced tax-law course. UCR's Public Economics, which analyses taxation economically, is already aligned to the comparator's introductory tax-law component above and cannot be matched twice; UCR offers no tax-law-doctrine course of any kind.

Both directly address notarial conflict resolution and negotiation: Pleitoefening offers an optional notarial track, Notariële conflictoplossing, focused on conflict analysis and negotiation; Negotiation & Strategic Thinking teaches BATNA/ZOPA analysis, interest-based negotiation and persuasive argument for reaching agreements.

Notariële ambtsuitoefening is a dedicated course on how a notary conducts their professional office. UCR's Negotiation & Strategic Thinking, which addresses professional negotiation practice, is already aligned to the comparator's pleading component above; UCR offers no course on notarial-office practice specifically.

Bachelorscriptie is the 6-EC independent bachelor research project (OER Article 9.1 requires 120 EC, including Juridische vaardigheden, before enrolment). No scheduled UCR course is a thesis; UCR's standardised Optional independent research element is shown in this row instead, consistent with researchComponentId.

notes.text: The Notarieel Recht bachelor is a professional academic Dutch-law degree, entirely compulsory (OER Article 10.2 and Articles 12.1-12.2 confirm no formal routes and no elective/minor space), combining a continuous jurisdiction-specific sequence in property, family, inheritance and matrimonial-property law, contract and obligations, company law, tax law, civil procedure/insolvency, criminal and public law, notarial professional practice and a bachelor thesis. At UCR, students can approach the same central notarial subject matter -- private law, property, business/corporate law and tax -- through UCR's law, business, economics, negotiation and communication courses. It does not teach Dutch inheritance law, matrimonial-property law, civil procedure, tax-law doctrine or notarial-office practice, and it does not lead to a Dutch notarial qualification. These pathways therefore compare related legal and commercial fields; UCR's programme approaches the notarial subject matter through related disciplines rather than reproducing the external notarial-law curriculum course by course.
